title: Console modular-fold and micro-workspace switcher — prototype & review
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: deliver a compact, context-aware console navigation pattern that reduces cognitive load on multi-workspace users and provides fast access to dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. This ticket scopes a modular 'fold' sidebar concept with a micro-workspace switcher (a lightweight, inline surface) and contextual flyouts for route-level controls (rollout toggles, cost breakdown quick-views, trace links). The prototype is intended for usability testing with Platform and two Product teams and to validate performance implications for rendering and keyboard nav.
acceptance_criteria: Macro: Users can switch workspaces within two clicks or one hotkey and remain in context for active route (dashboard/rollout/cost),
Micro: Compact-fold preserves primary routes with stable positioning across window widths down to 960px,
Rollout lens: A 1-click canary toggle and quick-metrics panel opens from the route flyout without a full route navigation,
Cost lens: Token-level cost preview surfaces for last 24h and allows 'open detailed view' to route to cost dashboard,
Accessibility: Keyboard navigation, focus order, and ARIA labels implemented for fold, micro-switcher, and flyout controls,
Performance: Prototype renders initial fold state under 120ms on a standard dev machine and lazy-loads heavy charts only on demand
updates: 2026-02-18: Initial PRD and low-fidelity flows posted. Defined scope to include rollout quick-flyout and token cost preview.
2026-02-24: Mid-fi wireframes reviewed with Platform PM (Jordan Reyes). Feedback: preserve stable visual anchor when fold toggles to avoid content shift.
2026-03-01: Hi-fi screens completed. Accessibility engineer (Samira Noor) flagged focus trap concern for micro-switcher; added keyboard escape behavior.

2026-03-05: Usability session #1 (6 participants from Search and Billing teams). Key findings: users appreciated quick metrics, requested clearer separation between global workspace context and route-specific controls.
2026-03-09: Implemented microcopy changes and revised flyout affordance to include subtle divider and motion affordance; updated Figma prototype.
2026-03-12: Design review with ENG (runtime) to discuss rendering constraints. Agreed on lazy-loading heavy charts and exposing a small metrics API endpoint for flyout use cases. Moving to In Review.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Reyes): Prefer a persistent breadcrumb in the header to avoid losing context when micro-switcher overlays small-screen layouts.
Engineering (Lina Gomez): Concern about initial paint cost for token-cost preview; recommended a lightweight aggregated metric endpoint (agreed).
Design Lead (Rafi Khatri): Love the modular fold concept; request added test plan for keyboard-only flows and screen reader narration samples.
Security (Priya Sen): No PII exposure in flyout metrics; verify logs generated for audit trail on rollout toggles.
usability_findings: Sessions: 6 users, task completion 83% for switch-and-view-cost scenario, average time 14s.
Pain: Some users attempted to drag the fold to resize — added affordance copy clarifying fold works as a mode not a resizable panel.
Opportunity: Introduce a hotkey overlay (Cmd+K style) shortcut to jump between workspaces and open last-used route.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Fold state could hide critical routes for novice users — Mitigation: persistent compact labels on hover and contextual onboarding tip.
Risk: Flyout metrics API increases load on telemetry backend — Mitigation: implement aggregated cache and 30s TTL for flyout endpoints.
next_steps: Finalize accessibility test scripts and schedule screen reader pass (owner: Samira Noor).
Ship prototype branch to staging with feature-flag for Platform and Billing teams (owner: Eng: Lina Gomez).
Collect 15 additional usability sessions focusing on multi-workspace power users and offline/poor-network conditions (owner: Maya).
Coordinate with Analytics to surface rollout quick-toggle metrics to the Console Observability dashboard.
